Sampled HR@10 with 99 negatives measures ranking within 100 candidates; it cannot establish full-catalog top-10 quality. Sampled metrics can even reverse model orderings in expectation ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). For this benchmark, retain pinned users, candidates and seeds. Proposed uncertainty protocol: store each model’s binary hit per user; bootstrap 200 users with replacement separately within each category, using identical resampled indices for both models; average the four category differences and report a 95% interval. This applies [paired bootstrap resampling](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html) to the fixed macro objective. One additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. Intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fixed candidates and trained models, excluding training-seed and negative-sampling variability.

Repeated architecture, hyperparameter and checkpoint selection can overfit validation noise; an ordinary bootstrap interval for the selected winner does not correct adaptive selection bias ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Practical protocol: predeclare candidate families, checkpoint frequency, stopping rules and tie handling; log every validation query; use paired differences as exploratory evidence, without claiming post-selection significance. Preserve all splits and leave final generalization assessment to the host’s independent held-out evaluation.

Compare search methods by equal cumulative GPU-seconds on matched hardware, rather than equal epochs: architectures and datasets have different epoch costs. HPO guidance recommends time-based budgets and performance-versus-budget traces ([Bischl et al.](https://wires.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/widm.1484)). Here, sum charged time across concurrent slots, including diagnostics and failed trials, within 43,200 GPU-seconds; report category scores, macro HR and incumbent-versus-budget curves. Equal-epoch comparisons can supplement this as training-dynamics evidence.
